messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-infer-gpu-pool-west2a - rule=cuda_alloc_fail_rate > 5% over 2m. Error sample: "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory". Affected hosts: gpu-west2a-{12,17,23}.
ops-sre: acked. i'm taking primary - will collect logs and triage.
alice: oncall here, adding context: downstream 5xx spike on /v1/generate from customers in region us-west2. throttling fallback to cpu-quant var started automatically.
ben: grabbing nvml logs now, running: `ssh gpu-west2a-12 sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 200 | grep -i cuda`
carmen: quick check of autoscaler - no scale events in last 10m. queue depth for the pool jumped 3x, latency SLO breached.
ops-sre: see repeated pattern: `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` then `cudaMalloc` OOMs. KV cache growth looks high for recent large-context requests. pushing a temporary kvcache eviction config now.
alice: can we proactively cordon one noisy host to stop noisy prefetch loops? recommends cordon gpu-west2a-23 and drain workloads there.
ben: cordon command sent: `kubectl cordon gpu-west2a-23 && kubectl drain gpu-west2a-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` - starting drain.
incident-bot: Note: automatic fallback route activated for tier=free -> model=redwood-quant-cpu to reduce pressure.
carmen: customer impact: 4 customer apps showing transient 500s (high-impact: edu-sso and chatflow). Support ticket ids linked.
alice: mitigation checklist: 1) cordon+drain noisy node (in progress) 2) reduce kvcache retention 3) bump dedicated-pool replica by +2 (if capacity available) 4) roll back recent prefetch change if present. executing 2 now.
ben: kvcache retention lowered via configmap patch. watching mem graphs. evictions spiked, fewer OOMs observed on the other hosts.
ops-sre: drain completed on gpu-west2a-23, 18 pods rescheduled gradually. observed one pod restart loop; killing and letting controller recreate.
carmen: autoscaler evaluation: quota has 2 spare GPUs in our region, requesting immediate scale-up of dedicated-pool using emergency burst; submitting request to resource manager.
alice: i'm notifying support to message affected customers with ETA ~20-30m for full recovery, advise retry/backoff.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by alice, severity=P2. Escalation path set to eng-runtime if metrics don't stabilize in 15m.
ops-sre: for postmortem: capture high-context request patterns, check whether a prompt engineering change caused kvcache blowup, and evaluate adding per-customer kvcache limits.
ben: current status: OOM rate down from 6.3% -> 1.1% in the last 4m after kvcache eviction + drain. latency trending down.
alice: keeping oncall loop open. if OOM rate <1% for next 10m we'll move to monitoring and close paging. assigning follow-ups: ben (logs+root-cause), carmen (capacity request / autoscale rules), ops-sre (runbook updates).
ops-sre: noted. I'll also add an alert suppression for noisy host rollover to avoid thrash.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert resolved automatically (conditions no longer met). Please confirm before closing the thread.
alice: confirmed - metrics stable. closing PD incident in 10m after final verification. thanks team :thumbsup:
ops-sre: adding timeline notes and screenshots to the incident ticket.
carmen: will draft customer update for support.
ben: copying key logs for postmortem: `grep -n "cudaMalloc failed" /var/log/inference/*.log | tail -n 50` and uploading to ticket.
alice: great. handoff to post-incident runbook tasks.
